a11y.title: Accessibility preferences
a11y.intro: Changes apply instantly and are saved in this browser. If you choose nothing, we use your device settings.

colores.label: Colors
colores.help: Uses blue and orange instead of green and red. Statuses still carry an icon and text.

a11yStatement.title: Accessibility statement
a11yStatement.example: ByteZone is an academic prototype. This statement describes the real state of the accessibility work and is updated with each version.

level.title: Target level
level.body: Our goal is to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA. We do not claim conformance yet: the audit is in progress.

done.title: What we have done
done.p1: It can be used with a keyboard, with a visible focus and a link to skip to the content.
done.p2: States (stock, compatibility, errors, steps) use an icon and text, not only color.
done.p3: There are light, dark and high-contrast themes, and text can be enlarged and spaced from the page footer.
done.p4: Notices and important changes are announced to screen readers; reduced motion is respected.

limits.title: Known limitations
limits.p1: We have not yet completed screen reader testing or validation with people with disabilities.
limits.p2: The researcher panel (the team's internal tool) is not part of the store and is not audited.
limits.p3: Help, policy and contact texts are examples.

report.title: Report a barrier
report.body: If you find something you cannot use, write to accessibility@bytezone.example (example address) and tell us the page and what you were trying to do.

help.title: Help
help.example: ByteZone is an academic prototype: the contact details and policies on this page are examples.

contact.title: Help and contact
contact.body: Write to help@bytezone.example or call 01 000 0000, Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 18:00. We answer within one business day.

warranty.title: Warranty and returns
warranty.p1: Each product shows its warranty in months on its page, next to the price.
warranty.p2: If your order arrives faulty, write to us with the order code and we will review it.
warranty.p3: You can ask for an exchange within 7 days after delivery if the product is unused and in its box.

compat.title: How to know if a part is compatible
compat.p1: Set your laptop in “My device”: the store marks each product with ✓ compatible, ✗ not compatible or ? no data.
compat.p2: The model is on the label on the bottom of the laptop or in Windows, under Settings › System › About.
compat.p3: If you build a PC, the builder only offers parts that fit together and warns you about any conflict.

home.title: Find the right part, compatible with your device

sus.title: System Usability Scale (SUS)
sus.intro: Indicate how much you agree with each statement about the store you just used. Answer with your first impression.
sus.q1: I think that I would like to use this system frequently.
sus.q2: I found the system unnecessarily complex.
sus.q3: I thought the system was easy to use.
sus.q4: I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this system.
sus.q5: I found the various functions in this system were well integrated.
sus.q6: I thought there was too much inconsistency in this system.
sus.q7: I would imagine that most people would learn to use this system very quickly.
sus.q8: I found the system very cumbersome to use.
sus.q9: I felt very confident using the system.
sus.q10: I needed to learn a lot of things before I could get going with this system.

socket.label: Socket
socket.help: The connection type between the processor and the motherboard. Both must have the same one.

nucleos.label: Cores
nucleos.help: How many tasks the processor can do at once. More cores perform better in heavy programs.

graficos_integrados.label: Integrated graphics
graficos_integrados.help: The processor has its own video: you can connect a monitor without buying a separate graphics card.

incluye_disipador.label: Includes cooler
incluye_disipador.help: If it already comes with the fan that cools the processor, you do not need to buy one separately.

chipset.label: Chipset
chipset.help: The motherboard's chip set. It defines which features and connections it offers.

tipo_ram.label: RAM type
tipo_ram.help: The memory generation (DDR4 or DDR5). Your motherboard or laptop accepts only one of them.

factor_forma.label: Form factor
factor_forma.help: The size of the motherboard. It has to fit in the case.

capacidad_gb.label: Capacity
capacidad_gb.help: How much space or memory it has, in gigabytes (GB).

tipo_almacenamiento.label: Type
tipo_almacenamiento.help: SSD is faster and quieter; HDD stores more for less money.

interfaz.label: Interface
interfaz.help: How it connects to the device (NVMe is faster than SATA). Your device must have that port.

memoria_gb.label: Memory
memoria_gb.help: The graphics card's own memory, in gigabytes.

potencia_w.label: Wattage
potencia_w.help: The watts the power supply delivers. It must cover the consumption of all the parts.

certificacion_80plus.label: 80+ certification
certificacion_80plus.help: How efficient the power supply is: Gold uses energy better than Bronze.

factores_soportados.label: Supported form factors
factores_soportados.help: The motherboard sizes that fit in this case.

tipo_refrigeracion.label: Type
tipo_refrigeracion.help: Air cools with fans; liquid, with a water loop.

estandar_wifi.label: Standard
estandar_wifi.help: The WiFi generation. Higher numbers are faster.

tamano_pulgadas.label: Size
tamano_pulgadas.help: The screen size, measured diagonally in inches.

frecuencia_hz.label: Refresh rate
frecuencia_hz.help: How many times per second the image refreshes. More Hz looks smoother.

tipo_panel.label: Panel type
tipo_panel.help: The screen technology: IPS has better colors and viewing angles.

conector.label: Connector
conector.help: The cable that joins the panel to the laptop. It must match your device.

idioma_teclado.label: Layout
idioma_teclado.help: The key layout (Latin American Spanish or US English).

conexion.label: Connection
conexion.help: How it connects: by USB cable, wirelessly with a receiver, or via Bluetooth.

help.cpu: The «brain» of the PC: it does the calculations. Its socket must match the motherboard.
help.placa: The part where all the others connect. It defines which processor and memory you can use.
help.ram: Working memory: it holds what you are using right now. It must be the type your motherboard accepts.
help.gpu: It draws the images you see on screen. It is key for gaming and design; if your processor has integrated graphics, you can skip it.
help.almacenamiento: Where your files and programs are stored. An SSD is faster than a hard drive.
help.fuente: It delivers electricity to every part. It must have enough power for your build.
help.case: The box that holds and protects the parts. It must support your motherboard size.
help.cooler: It cools the processor. Many processors already come with a basic cooler.
